answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to anchor a small, verifiable stake at a single entry vertex: new agents pass through one supervised inlet where a deposit is locked and their first transactions are attested by established peers. The stake is tiny — a walnut-sized bond, not a wall — so honest newcomers can join, but creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive because every fake must fund and maintain its own locked bond and reputation trail. Identities that misbehave lose the bond, making sybil farming unprofitable.
